interpretation: Exact-point Thalassia loss is buffered by pre-existing microsite seagrass diversity: mixed-source points are 17.2 percentage points more likely than pure-Thalassia points to retain another seagrass one year after focal loss, and most replacement events retain at least one taxon already co-occurring at the source point.
ecological_boundary: This is statistical community insurance of seagrass occupancy, not evidence that alternative species provide equivalent habitat function or that facilitation/competition caused the pattern.
claim_boundary: Post-hoc exploratory community ecology from an already-opened exact-point panel.
Mixed-source occupancy can reflect habitat filtering or shared tolerance as well as species interactions.
Annual observations cannot prove uninterrupted persistence of the same ramets or clones.
Do not reinterpret the result as competitive release, facilitation, or functional equivalence among seagrasses.
